proof_summary: Letting \(P(n)=\sum_{k=1}^n\gcd(k,n)\), use its multiplicativity and \(P(p)=2p-1\) for primes to evaluate the squarefree composite \(N=3\cdot37\cdot43\cdot42307\cdot116341=23492890653051\). This gives \(P(N)=610815156979325\) and \(1+P(N)=26N\), so the defining gcd equals \(N\) and hence \(a(N)=1\) despite \(N\) being composite.
